The crash occurs at the auth service’s `Emitter` check in [service.go](/app/lib/service/service.go:1012). When multiple audit URIs are configured, `initExternalLog` returns a `MultiLog`, but [MultiLog](/app/lib/events/multilog.go:29) does not implement `EmitAuditEvent`. A single `stdout://` backend has the same problem: it creates a [WriterLog](/app/lib/service/service.go:904), which supports only legacy emission.

The likely fix spans [emitter.go](/app/lib/events/emitter.go), [multilog.go](/app/lib/events/multilog.go), and [service.go](/app/lib/service/service.go): add `WriterEmitter` with newline-delimited JSON emission and trace errors; validate and fan out emitters in `NewMultiLog`; propagate its new error return; and use `WriterEmitter` for stdout. Close handling needs care because `WriterLog.Close` already closes its writer, so closing both could close it twice.

Existing tests cover audit URI list parsing, but I found no test of multiple backend startup or stdout emission. The reported error strongly supports this diagnosis; runtime behavior remains unverified. I updated [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). The higher-priority fault-localization instruction prohibited project source and test edits, so I did not implement the fix.

Fixed the auth service crash for multiple audit backends. `MultiLog` now validates and fans out audit events, and `stdout://` uses the new `WriterEmitter` to write newline-delimited JSON.

Added tests for emission, close behavior, and mixed URI initialization. `go test ./lib/events ./lib/service` and `git diff --check` pass.

VERDICT: ACCEPT

[WriterEmitter](/app/lib/events/emitter.go) provides JSON event output and closes its writer; [MultiLog](/app/lib/events/multilog.go) validates emitters and fans out events; [service.go](/app/lib/service/service.go) uses the new emitter for `stdout://`.
